title: Coral and the Terminal
premise: Navigator Ines Vasquez serves aboard the Coral, a salvage hauler whose hold holds the cryo-preserved backups of a colony that died two centuries ago — backups the crew is contractually forbidden to wake. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct since that same colony's fall, Ines realizes the sleepers may not be dead at all. Racing to a relay at the edge of dead space, Ines discovers the Coral's owners engineered the colony's death and have been hunting the survivors' descendants ever since; waking the backups would expose everything. Torn between duty to the ship that raised them and love for Juno, the comms officer who first decoded the signal, Ines must choose truth over loyalty — broadcasting the archive and waking the sleepers as the Coral's corporate masters close in. The novel ends with the relay burning behind them, the awakened colonists scattered into free space, and Ines and Juno adrift but finally unowned.
about_author: Y. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one answered before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose name they decline to share, on the theory that some signals are better kept faint.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Ines navigates the Coral through a decaying shipping lane while cataloguing the cryo-backups in the hold, a ritual they perform against regulations. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the sense of carrying the dead who might not be dead.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Captain Oyelaran reviews the Coral's charter with Ines: the backups belong to Meridian Combine, and interference means forfeiture of everything, including life support rights. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the weight of obligation; loyalty presented as survival.

chapters.title: A Voice in Extinct Tongue
chapters.summary: Juno, the comms officer, intercepts a repeating distress signal in Kessari — a language extinct for two centuries, the tongue of the lost colony Veyra Station. She secretly asks Ines to help decode it. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Dream
chapters.summary: Ines cross-references the signal against the backup manifests and finds a match: the distress call predates the colony's recorded death by eleven years. Someone was calling for help before anyone admitted there was danger. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovered lies.

chapters.title: Course Correction
chapters.summary: Oyelaran orders the Coral away from the signal's origin toward a routine salvage. Ines falsifies a minor nav log to buy time — their first act of betrayal against the ship. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: guilt braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Juno's Grammar of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Juno reconstructs enough Kessari to translate fragments: 'the relay still listens,' 'we are not finished.' She and Ines grow closer over long night shifts, translating a dead people's last words. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in secrecy; love beginning.

chapters.title: Meridian Calls
chapters.summary: A Meridian Combine auditor boards at a fueling station, asking pointed questions about the hold's integrity and the crew's communications traffic. Oyelaran covers for Ines — or seems to. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: menace under courtesy; the captain's divided face shown for the first time.

chapters.title: Dead Space Ahead
chapters.summary: The Coral enters the region charts simply mark DEAD SPACE, where the relay sits. Navigation instruments degrade; Ines must fly by memory and instinct, feeling the sleepers' presence below like ballast. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: isolation sharpened into focus.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the ancient relay and find it maintained — recently. Fresh power couplings, new seals. Someone alive has been keeping a two-hundred-year-old promise. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an intruder.

chapters.title: Descendants
chapters.summary: Contact: a scavver clan descended from Veyra survivors, hiding in the debris fields, still transmitting in Kessari on the chance anyone remembers them. Their matriarch, Sefa, recognizes the Coral's registry — and flinches. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: wary hospitality; old wounds meeting new faces.

chapters.title: Sefa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sefa tells the true history: Meridian didn't lose Veyra Station; it sold the colony's air, then erased the records and hunted the survivors to keep the crime buried. The backups in the Coral's hold are evidence — and hostages. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: grief delivered as testimony; the theme of truth versus loyalty made explicit.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oyelaran reveals she has known for years; her silence bought the crew's wages and the ship's license. She orders Ines to hand over Juno's decodes and sever contact with the clan. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: corruption framed as care — power protecting itself by protecting its servants.

chapters.title: Confession in the Hold
chapters.summary: Ines confesses everything to Juno among the sleeper pods, including their forged logs and their childhood debt to the Coral. Juno doesn't forgive so much as refuse to let Ines carry it alone. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallized; the relationship becomes the story's spine.

chapters.title: The Auditor Returns
chapters.summary: The Meridian auditor reappears — aboard a gunship, with authority to scuttle the Coral and everyone aboard. Oyelaran stalls; the crew splits between obedience and mutiny. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: the walls closing in; loyalty fracturing along fault lines.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ines calculates a window: the relay can broadcast the full archive — proof of Meridian's crime and the waking codes for the backups — but only during a twenty-two-hour alignment. After that, the relay dies forever. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: a clock starts; dread becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Mutiny, Gently
chapters.summary: Ines asks the crew, one by one, rather than seizing the ship. Engineer Bao, medic Ilsa, and half the watch join; the rest stand down without fighting. Oyelaran locks herself in the bridge. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — not to the ship or its owners, but to each other.

chapters.title: What Oyelaran Kept
chapters.summary: Juno talks her way onto the bridge and finds Oyelaran guarding a final secret: her own daughter is among the sleepers, woken once and put back when Meridian threatened the crew. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as the story's first victim; pity without absolution.

chapters.title: Alignment
chapters.summary: The broadcast begins. The relay pours the archive into every open channel while Ines flies the Coral through Meridian interdiction fire to keep the transmitter aimed. Juno narrates the transmission live in Kessari and Standard both. POV: alternating Ines/Juno. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, precision, and defiance fused.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: With the codes loose, the clan and the crew open the pods together. The sleepers surface into a universe that forgot them, greeted by strangers speaking their language badly and meaning it completely. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: resurrection as communal act; grief and joy indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Gunship's Silence
chapters.summary: The archive reaches Meridian's own crews; the gunship stands down as its officers receive orders no one will acknowledge in writing. Power, exposed, retreats. Oyelaran surrenders the bridge to Ines without a word. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: anticlimax as victory — corruption undone not by force but by witness.

chapters.title: Scattering
chapters.summary: The awakened colonists choose their own destinations across free space; Sefa offers Ines and Juno a place among the clans, and they accept — not as rescuers, but as family. The Coral's charter burns in the recycler. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: release; identity rebuilt outside ownership.

chapters.title: Coral, Unregistered
chapters.summary: Months later, the renamed Coral runs honest routes past the dead relay, which Ines leaves powered down at last — its work finished. In the hold, where the pods used to be, the crew keeps a garden. Final line: a signal sent out in Kessari, just to say we remember. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: resolution — truth kept, love kept, nothing owned.
